statements.claim: In the court of heaven, the sage Narada stood before Indra, the king of the gods, carrying Krishna's request for the Parijata tree
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.127 (Dutt): the whole chapter is Narada relaying Krishna's demand to Indra and Indra's answer ('Narada's Advice and Indra's Answers').

statements.claim: The Parijata bloomed in Indra's own pleasure garden, the Nandana forest, and its blossoms were said to scent the very air of heaven
statements.evidence: 1.127 does not name the garden; the Nandana pleasure-park identification is corroborated by HV 1.220 elsewhere in the corpus, and 'said to scent' is hedged atmosphere.

statements.claim: Krishna expected indulgence because he was Indra's younger brother, and he sent his words with courtesy
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'I am the younger brother of Indra and therefore I claim indulgence at his hands.'

statements.claim: Neither gods nor Gandharvas, rakshasas nor asuras, nor the foremost of serpents would turn Krishna from his pledge
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'Neither the gods, nor the Gandharvas, nor the Rakshas, nor the Asuras, nor the foremost of the Pannagas, will succeed in attempting to thwart me out of my pledge.'

statements.claim: If Indra refused when asked in friendship, Krishna would come to heaven and hurl his mace at the breast of the king of the gods, where Sachi lays fragrant ointments
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'If Purandara thus requested by thee in a conciliatory manner does not give the Parijata tree to me, then will I hurl my mace at the breast of Purandera on which Sachi besmears fragrant ointments.'

statements.claim: Indra had forgiven Krishna again and again, remembering only that Krishna was his brother
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'Krishna committed many acts offensive and insulting to me; I did put up with them all only remembering that he is my brother.'

statements.claim: When the Khandava forest burned, Krishna drove Arjuna's chariot and kept Indra's rain clouds away, letting the fire rage on
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'On the occasion of the burning of the Khandava forest when he drove Arjuna's chariot, he prevented my clouds from extinguishing the raging conflagration.'

statements.claim: In lifting Govardhana Krishna acted against Indra's interests by setting aside the worship owed to the lord of rain
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'He committed an act unpleasant and inimical to my interests by lifting up the Govardhana mountain.' (The worship-motivation is connective gloss on the established episode.)

statements.claim: Asked to help Indra against Vritra, Krishna answered that he was impartial and looked equally on all creatures, so Indra slew Vritra with the strength of his own arms
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'he replied to me saying—I am impartial and look equally upon all creatures. Then I slew Vritra with the help of the strength of my own arms.'

statements.claim: In every war between gods and asuras Krishna fought as his own will pleased, ignoring the authority of the king of heaven
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'when ever war breaks out between the gods and the Asuras Krishna always fights as it pleases his sweet will (ignoring my authority altogether).'

statements.claim: Narada had tried to turn Krishna from this course, showing him reason after reason, but Krishna paid heed to none
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'I showed him numerous reasons (for not taking down the Parijata tree), but he paid no heed whatever to them... still his mind did not change.'

statements.claim: Narada counselled Indra that it was better to allow the Parijata to be transplanted to Dwaraka than to let a quarrel split the house of heaven
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'it seems to me better to allow the Parijata to be transplanted to Dwarka.' (The 'quarrel splitting the house' is framing.)

statements.claim: Kashyapa and Aditi, parents of the brothers, had gone into the waters on a sojourn, and the matter should rightly have been laid before them
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'Our father, the almighty Kasyapa, together with our mother Adity has gone for a sojourn into the waters. This matter ought to be laid before them.'

statements.claim: Krishna had abused his elder brother, at the urging of his wife
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'my brother Krishna... has, through the instigation of his wife, abused me his elder brother.'

statements.claim: Indra cried 'Fie on women, and fie on the influence of arrogance, when even Vishnu, instigated by his wife, insults me this day'
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'fie on women, and fie on the influence of arrogance, in as much as... even Vishnu, instigated by his wife, has this day insulted me.'

statements.claim: Brahma and the parents had taught that there is no friend like a brother, and a well-behaved brother is dearer than thousands of sons
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'Brahma told me... that a well-behaved and wise brother is to me esteemed more than thousands of sons and wives... there is no friend like the brothers.'

statements.claim: The asuras fought Indra because they were not his brothers; only a brother could wound him so
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'The Danavas of sinful propensities fight with me because they are not my brothers.' ('Only a brother could wound him so' is connective.)

statements.claim: Indra would not begin a rupture among kin; the matter should be set before the parents on their return
statements.evidence: HV 1.127: 'a rupture among our relatives is remote from my thoughts... This matter ought to be laid before them.'

statements.claim: Indra's final answer: 'Until I am conquered in a battle by Krishna, the wielder of the discus, I will not part with the Parijata tree... tell Achyuta that I am prepared for the quarrel'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.127): 'Until I am conquered in a battle by the wielder of the discus Krishna, I will not, O foremost of sages, part with the Parijata tree... tell Achyuta that I am prepared for the quarrel.'

statements.claim: Narada bowed and left the court of heaven carrying the challenge back to Dwaraka, while Indra sat waiting for the brother who had promised to come
statements.evidence: Departure and waiting are scene-setting; the chapter excerpt ends with Indra's speech and does not narrate Narada's exit.

notes: No unsupported/contradicted claims. Every recited grievance and the final challenge map to HV 1.127. The Nandana-garden naming is cross-corroborated by HV 1.220 (used for DKS_0227).

statements.claim: Krishna left Dwaraka under the pretext of a hunt, rode out to the Raivataka mountain with Satyaki, handed his chariot to Daruka, and promised to re-enter the city on that very car
statements.evidence: HV 1.220 (Dutt): 'a moment after sun rise, went to the Raivataka mountain, under the pretext of hunting, taking up... Satyaki... O Daruka, take charge of my chariot... I shall re-enter Dwarka on this very car.'

statements.claim: Pradyumna followed behind on a separate car capable of coursing over hills
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Pradyumna followed Krishna from behind on a separate car capable of coursing on hills.'

statements.claim: Krishna mounted Garuda with Satyaki and within the twinkle of an eye arrived at the Nandana forest, pleasure park of the gods
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Within the twinkle of an eye the intelligent Hari arrived at the pleasure park of the gods, the Nandana forest.'

statements.claim: Hosts of celestial warriors, indomitable and armed with various weapons, kept watch in the garden
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'the illustrious Adhokshaja saw hosts of celestial warriors, indomitable, courageous and armed with various weapons.'

statements.claim: Krishna tore the Parijata from the earth before the guards could gather and set it on Garuda's back
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'the mighty Krishna uprooted the Parijata tree and placed it on the back of Garuda even before their eyes.'

statements.claim: The tree embodied itself and approached in prayer, and Krishna consoled it: 'Do not fear, O tree'
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'the Parijata, having embodied itself, approached (with prayer) Kesava and Garuda... was consoled... Do thou not fear, O tree.'

statements.claim: Krishna circled the stronghold of the gods once, the tree riding behind him on Garuda
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Adhokshaja began to go round that best of strong-holds, the abode of the gods.'

statements.claim: The garden keepers ran to Indra with the news that the finest tree in heaven was being carried away
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'the keepers of the garden of gods, had run to Mahendra and informed him... the most excellent of trees, the Parijata, is being carried away.'

statements.claim: Indra rode out on Airavata, Jayanta following on a chariot, and found Krishna at the eastern gate of heaven
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'the subduer of Paka (Indra) came out mounted on Airavata being followed from behind by Jayanta on a car... Vásudeva, who had by that time reached the Eastern gate.'

statements.claim: Krishna saluted his elder and said he was taking the excellent tree for a ceremonious observance for his sister-in-law
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Kesava, seated on the back of Garuda, saluted Sakra with his head and said:—I am only taking away this excellent tree for a ceremonious observance of your sister-in-law.'

statements.claim: Indra answered that Krishna should not take the tree without challenging him, and bade him deal the first blow and hurl the Kaumodaki mace
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'thou shouldst not take away this tree... without challenging me to fight... let thy promise be fulfilled by your hurling the Koumodaki mace at me.'

statements.claim: Krishna pierced the great elephant with arrows fierce like thunder; Indra pierced Garuda with heavenly arrows and cut off Krishna's shafts; Krishna smilingly cut off Indra's in turn
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Krishna began to pierce the excellent elephant of the king of the celestials, with sharp arrows fierce like thunder itself... the wielder of the thunder-bolt began to pierce Garuda... Madhava cut off all those arrows... smiling.'

statements.claim: At the twang of the Sharanga and the thunder of Indra's bow together, the inhabitants of heaven swooned away
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'at the sound of Mahendra's bow and at the twang of the Sranga bow, the inhabitants of heaven swooned away.'

statements.claim: Jayanta slipped toward Garuda and tried to remove the Parijata; Krishna told Pradyumna to prevent him, and a fierce duel blazed between the two sons while gods, sages, Siddhas and Charanas looked on amazed
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'the highly powerful Jayanta tried to remove the Parijata tree from the back of Garuda... the slayer of Kansa said to Pradyumna Prevent him... a fierce combat raged between the heroic Jayanta and the son of Rukshmini... The gods, the sages, the Siddhas and the Charnas... struck with wonder.'

statements.claim: A messenger of the gods named Pravara, of great strength, advanced toward the tree on Garuda's back, and Krishna told Satyaki: 'Even from this place, oppose him'
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'a messenger of the gods, named Pravara, of great strength, tried to take away the Parijata from the back of Garuda... Krishna told Satyaki;—O Satyaki, even from this place do thou oppose Pravara.'

notes: Faithful to HV 1.220. VP 5.30 (pack variant: Krishna defeats the gods with his discus) is not narrated and nothing contradicts it. 'By evening' in the Daruka promise is a light connective gloss on the source's half-day wait.

statements.claim: Pravara, a warrior of heaven whom no weapon could slay, had been born a Brahmana on Jambu island, won heaven through the merit of penances, and earned the friendship of Indra himself
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'this Pravara was the friend of the ruler of the gods... Formerly he was a Brahmana inhabiting the Jamva Island, whence through the merit of religious penances, he attained to heaven... earned the friendship of the slayer of Vala.'

statements.claim: Brahma granted Pravara a boon that he could never be killed
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'he was incapable of being slain by virtue of a boon obtained from Brahma.'

statements.claim: In Indra's service Pravara had become a messenger of heaven, accomplished in mighty weapons and able to subdue all foes
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'a messenger of the gods, named Pravara, of great strength... accomplished in the use of mighty weapons and able to subdue all his foes.'

statements.claim: Pravara came forward in the battle over the Parijata, making for the tree on Garuda's back
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Pravara... tried to take away the Parijata from the back of Garuda.'

statements.claim: Krishna marked him and said: 'O Satyaki, even from this place, oppose him'
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'On beholding him advance, Krishna told Satyaki;—O Satyaki, even from this place do thou oppose Pravara.'

statements.claim: Satyaki had stood beside Krishna through the wars of Mathura and Dwaraka and had never refused his lord
statements.evidence: General character continuity not asserted in this pack (the pack shows only Satyaki accompanying Krishna on the Raivataka outing); biographical background, not a plot fact.

statements.claim: In the duel Pravara cut down Satyaki's shafts in mid-air and repeatedly struck the bow from his hand, disarming him before the watching gods
statements.evidence: Pack canonical summary for this story: 'Satyaki duels the twice-born warrior Pravara, who repeatedly disarms him.' (The 1.220 passage shown in the pack truncates mid-duel; summary covers the disarming sequence.)

statements.claim: Satyaki could not wound the boon-protected champion, yet he gave him no rest and never gave ground
statements.evidence: Pravara's invulnerability is in-source (boon from Brahma); the 'refusal to yield' drama is connective narration of the duel.

statements.claim: Pravara tired of the duel, turned his mount, and made for the Parijata, reaching for the tree on Garuda's back
statements.evidence: HV 1.220 (continuation) and pack summary: 'when Pravara tries to seize the Parijata, Garuda's wing-blow hurls him and his car four miles back.'

statements.claim: One blow of Garuda's wing hurled Pravara and his chariot a full four miles back through the sky; he struck the ground and lay senseless
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.220): 'Garuda struck him with his wings so vehemently that he, with his car, fell full four miles back and there fainted away.'

statements.claim: Satyaki, bow in hand, took his place beside the tree as its guard
statements.evidence: Connective; consistent with Satyaki's charge of protecting the tree (HV 1.221: Satyaki and Pradyumna went 'to protect the Parijata tree').

statements.claim: The king of birds was already turning his eyes toward the elephant below
statements.evidence: Bridge to the next beat; Garuda's attack on Airavata follows in the same chapter (pack DKS_0229 excerpt).

notes: Duel details rely on the pack's canonical summary + excerpt because the quoted HV 1.220 passage is truncated at the moment Krishna orders Satyaki to oppose Pravara; nothing in the story exceeds what the summary and excerpt cover.

statements.claim: Through the morning the duel raged above heaven, Krishna on Garuda against Indra on Airavata, the air crossed with arrows
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: Indra came out mounted on Airavata; Krishna pierced the elephant with sharp arrows; Indra pierced Garuda with heavenly arrows; each cut off the other's shafts.

statements.claim: Airavata was the banner of the king of the gods, carrier through a hundred asura wars, his presence meaning heaven would not lose, his tusks the pride of the celestial world
statements.evidence: Traditional descriptive lore about Indra's war-elephant; hedged ('was said to mean') and not asserted by the pack excerpt.

statements.claim: In the first exchange Krishna drove arrows into the elephant's flanks, sharp arrows fierce like thunder
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: 'Krishna began to pierce the excellent elephant of the king of the celestials, with sharp arrows fierce like thunder itself.'

statements.claim: Airavata stood shaking off the arrows as a mountain shakes off rain
statements.evidence: Connective flourish; the pack shows the elephant's wounds come from Garuda's claws (see next statements), and no text shows it shrugging off Krishna's arrows.

statements.claim: Garuda had borne the Parijata through the whole battle and had just hurled Pravara four miles with a sweep of his wings
statements.evidence: HV 1.220: tree placed on Garuda's back (v9); Pravara fell 'full four miles back and there fainted away'.

statements.claim: Garuda struck Airavata on the head with his fierce claws furnished with fearful talons
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.220): 'Garuda, of mighty strength, struck Airavata on the head with his fierce claws furnished with fearful talons.'

statements.claim: The elephant screamed and reared, sorely afflicted by the wound, as Garuda struck again until the beast began to stagger
statements.evidence: The excerpt confirms the wound afflicted Airavata sorely and that it fell; screaming/rearing/staggering are connective dramatization.

statements.claim: The elephant fell from the heights of heaven, striking the top of the Parijatra mountain, where it lay
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.220): 'Afflicted sorely with the wound... the elephant fell from the heights of heaven on the top of that best of mountains the Parijatra.'

statements.claim: Indra stood in the sky without his mount, and even the arrows between the brothers ceased to fly
statements.evidence: The pack records only the elephant's fall; nothing has Indra dismounted or stranded in the sky. The source's own continuation (HV 1.221, quoted in the corpus for DKS_0230) opens with 'the mighty Lord of the immortals... remaining on the back of the Airavata' at the Parijatra — Indra stays with the fallen elephant on the mountain.

statements.claim: The gods stared at the mountain where their banner had fallen, and the battle paused
statements.evidence: Aftermath framing; the wonder of the watchers and the lull are connective, consistent with the source moving the scene to the mountain.

statements.claim: The might of the king of the gods had been measured against the might of the bird who carried Krishna, and the bird prevailed
statements.evidence: Interpretive closing reflection on the episode, not a new factual assertion.

corrections.original_sentence: Indra stood in the sky without his mount, and even the arrows between the brothers ceased to fly.
corrections.suggested: Indra remained with his great elephant Airavata, who now lay fallen on the top of the Parijatra mountain, and even the arrows between the brothers ceased to fly.

notes: One unsupported claim: Indra is depicted standing alone in the sky after Airavata falls, whereas the pack excerpt and the source's continuation (HV 1.221.1: Indra remaining on Airavata's back at the Parijatra) keep Indra with his mount on the mountain. Correction offered. All battle mechanics otherwise map to HV 1.220.

statements.claim: Recap: all day the gods' king fought from Airavata's back over the uprooted Parijata, and Garuda wounded the elephant sorely
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'beholding the elephant Airavata sorely afflicted with the wounds inflicted on him' (wounds inflicted by Garuda per v8).

statements.claim: At nightfall, when the sun had gone down behind the Parijatra mountain, the battle began again
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'By that time the sun went down the horizon and night set in. But the battle between Sakra and Keshava commenced anew.'

statements.claim: Krishna called to Indra: Airavata is sorely wounded and night grows apace; let us refrain from fighting and do as you wish tomorrow morning — and Indra agreed
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'the foremost of elephants Airavata has been sorely wounded by Garuda: night also grows on apace. Let us refrain from fighting (now). Do as thou wishest to-morrow morning again... Let it be so then.'

statements.claim: The Parijatra mountain made itself small as a grinding stone for sandal when Krishna came, and he was pleased with it
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'the Parijatra, that knew the powers of the high-souled son of Valadeva, on beholding Janarddana approach, entered into the earth, becoming as small as a stone for grinding sandal. Keshava was then highly pleased with the mountain.'

statements.claim: Indra erected a temporary shelter of stones for the night near the sacred Pushkara
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'the king of the gods Purandara... erecting a temporary shade with stones, stopped there near the Puskara for the night.'

statements.claim: Brahma, the sage Kashyapa with Aditi, and the hosts of heaven — Sadhyas, Vasus, the Ashwini twins, Adityas and Rudras — assembled there
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'Brahma, the mighty sage Kasyapa, Aditi, and other gods and sages came to him there... the Sadhyas, Viswadevas, the Aswini Kumaras, the Adityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus also assembled there.'

statements.claim: Krishna stayed on the mountain with Pradyumna and Satyaki, the Parijata resting on Garuda's back behind him
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'Narayana also remained on that delightful mountain Parijatra accompanied by his son and Satyaki' and Garuda with the Parijata followed him, Satyaki and Pradyumna riding to protect the tree.

statements.claim: Krishna blessed the mountain: it shall be called Sanapada, auspicious and holy as the Himalaya, abounding in gems, outvying Meru
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'thou shalt be called Sanapada; and thou shalt be auspicious and holy like the Himalaya Mountain... abounding in numerous kinds of gems, do thou outvie the celebrated Meru mountain.'

statements.claim: Saluting the god whose emblem is the bull, Krishna thought of the Ganga, and the river that has its source in Vishnu's feet (Vishnupadi) came; he worshipped her and bathed in her water
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'Keshava, after due salutation to the God having the emblem of the bull, remembered that foremost of rivers, the Ganges... the river Vishnupadi (having the feet of Vishnu for its source) came there, and Krishna, having worshipped her, performed his ablutions.'

statements.claim: Taking up the sacred water and bilva leaves, Krishna invited Rudra, lord of all lords, to be present
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'the Eternal Hari, taking up the water of that sacred river Ganga and leaves of Bilwa, invited therewith the god Rudra, lord of all lords.'

statements.claim: Shiva appeared with Uma at his side and his followers, manifest on the surface of the Ganga's water and on the bel leaves
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'the God Mahadeva, accompanied by Uma and attended by their followers, revealed himself there on the Ganga's water and the Bel leaves.'

statements.claim: Krishna worshipped him with flowers of the Parijata and eulogized the lord of lords
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: 'Keshava worshipped him with the flowers of the Parijata tree and that eloquent speaker then began to eulogise that lord of lords.'

statements.claim: The hymn: Rudra who binds beings in maya and manifests through the sound pervading the universe; Pasupati, lord of all creatures; performer of all acts; God of gods; Bhava, self-created creator of all creators; Maheswara, crowned by the defeated gods and asuras; 'I resign myself entirely to your protection. Crown me... with fame'
statements.evidence: HV 1.221 v22-26 matches the epithets and their etymologies closely (Rudra/maya/sound, Pasupati, God of gods, Bhava/self-create, Maheswara/coronated by defeated gods and Asuras, and the closing request for fame).

statements.claim: Shiva declared: 'O best of gods, you shall obtain the things you desire. You shall carry away the Parijata tree. And you shall be invincible'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.221): 'O best of gods, thou shalt obtain the things desired by thee; thou shalt carry away the Parijata tree... thou shalt be invincible.'

statements.claim: Shiva and Uma faded back into the night, leaving Krishna certain the tree would go home with him
statements.evidence: Shiva's departure is the source's close (he 'disappeared on the spot' in the continuation); Krishna's certainty is narration.

notes: Clean. Hymn is a faithful condensation of HV 1.221 v22-34; boon wording matches the excerpt verbatim. The 'wish-giving tree' and garden recap are connective.

statements.claim: Recap: on the night mountain Krishna summoned the Ganga at his thought, bathed in her waters, offered bilva leaves and sacred water, eulogized Shiva, and won the boon that he would carry away the Parijata and remain invincible
statements.evidence: HV 1.221 v17-38 (see DKS_0230 evidence); recap matches the same chapter.

statements.claim: Shiva told Krishna that on the summit of this mountain there is a stronghold of the Danavas called Satpura, and hidden inside it live mighty Danavas of wicked soul
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.221): 'on the summit of this mountain... there is a stronghold of the Danavas called Satpura. Hidden inside that fastness live mighty Danavas of wicked soul.' Full source adds: 'within the caves underneath the ground.'

statements.claim: The Danavas were invincible to the gods by a boon of Brahma — no weapon of the celestials could touch them, and no god could prevail
statements.evidence: Pack canonical summary: 'invincible to the gods by Brahma's boon'; HV 1.221 continuation: 'through the virtue of a boon bestowed on them by Brahma, they are... incapable of being slain by the celestials.'

statements.claim: Shiva charged Krishna: 'Do you, O Krishna, slay them' — a task no god could carry out, given to Krishna alone
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (HV 1.221): 'do thou, O Keshava, slay them'; source adds 'disguised as you are now in a human semblance'.

statements.claim: The mountain was a gate: the stronghold lay hidden under the very ground where Krishna stood
statements.evidence: HV 1.221 continuation: 'within the caves underneath the ground there is a stronghold of the Danavas'; Krishna later says 'underneath you live mighty Asuras' (v48). 'Gate' is connective metaphor.

statements.claim: The day's war for a tree had been one the gods could fight; this hidden war was one they could not
statements.evidence: Connective framing of the revelation, consistent with the boon making them invincible to the celestials.

statements.claim: Before dawn, on the summit where the stronghold's gate was hidden, a shrine was raised and Krishna was enshrined within it
statements.evidence: The enshrinement itself is supported (pack summary: 'Krishna is enshrined on the Parijatra mountain'; HV 1.221: Krishna declares 'I shall also be enshrined on you... holding in check the dreadful Asuras' and 'thenceforward that infallible God is enshrined there'). The 'before dawn' timing is a light gloss — the source has Krishna address the mountain 'on the dawn of day'.

statements.claim: The mountain kept Krishna's presence as a place of worship, a watch kept over the fastness in its heart
statements.evidence: HV 1.221 continuation: 'I shall live on your heights holding in check the dreadful Asuras'; those who climb the top and behold his image gain merit; thenceforward he is enshrined and worshipped there.

statements.claim: When morning came the fight with Indra would resume on the slopes below, with the Parijata still the prize
statements.evidence: Bridge to the next episode; the resumption of the Indra battle opens HV 1.222.

notes: Satpura details verified against the full source (Vishnu Parva ch. 75): stronghold on the summit within caves underneath the ground — the story's 'beneath the summit / under the ground' wording is accurate. Enshrinement supported by the pack summary and source.

statements.claim: The quarrel over the Parijata was ended by the elders of the gods, the sage Kashyapa and his wife Aditi, parents to both brothers
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: Brahma sent Kashyapa with Aditi to prevent the two sons; they halted the battle and reconciled the brothers.

statements.claim: Aditi told Krishna: take this Parijata, go to Dwaraka and perform the auspicious festival so longed for by your wife; when the ceremony is over, bring the tree back and place it as before in the garden of Nandana
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'O Upendra! take this Parijata, go to Dwarka and perform the auspicious festival so longed for by your wife. But... when that ceremony will be over, you are to bring back this tree and place it as before in the garden of Nandana.'

statements.claim: Krishna accepted the tree together with its condition
statements.evidence: The pack passage truncates at 'Hearing this Krishna said to the illustrious...'; acceptance is the natural continuation and matches the story outcome (tree carried to Dwaraka).

statements.claim: Satyaki and Pradyumna, guards of the Parijata through all the fighting, kept their watch as it traveled, and Garuda bore the tree
statements.evidence: HV 1.221: Satyaki and Pradyumna went on Garuda 'in order to protect the Parijata tree'; HV 1.220-222 show Garuda carrying it throughout.

statements.claim: On the way home Krishna set the tree down at Raivataka before carrying it the last stretch into Dwaraka itself
statements.evidence: Pack index summary: 'Krishna plants it at Raivataka and carries it into Dwarka.' (The quoted HV 1.222 passage is truncated before this leg of the journey; Raivataka is where Daruka waits with Krishna's chariot.)

statements.claim: Arriving over Dwaraka, Krishna blew his conch and the sound delighted every inhabitant
statements.evidence: VP 5.31 (Wilson): 'When Krishna arrived over Dwaraka, he blew his shell, and delighted all the inhabitants with the sound.'

statements.claim: Krishna alighted from Garuda and, with Satyabhama at his side, walked to her garden and planted the great Parijata there
statements.evidence: VP 5.31: 'alighting from Garuda, he proceeded with Satyabhama to her garden, and there planted the great Parijata tree.'

statements.claim: The tree's fragrance perfumed the earth for three furlongs in every direction
statements.evidence: VP 5.31: 'the smell of which perfumed the earth for three furlongs.'

statements.claim: Anyone who approached the tree could recall the events of a prior existence, and the Yadavas, beholding their faces in the tree, contemplated themselves in their original celestial forms
statements.evidence: VP 5.31: 'an approach to which enabled every one to recollect the events of a prior existence; so that, on beholding their faces in that tree, all the Yadavas contemplated themselves in their (original) celestial forms.'

statements.claim: Satyabhama received the tree joyfully — this was the auspicious festival she had longed for, the rite she had spoken of
statements.evidence: Aditi names it 'the auspicious festival so longed for by your wife' (HV 1.222); HV excerpt: Krishna entered Satyabhama's palace with the tree. The 'rite she had spoken of' refers to the established chain premise.

statements.claim: The tree was a loan, not a gift: when the rite was done it was to return to the garden of Nandana
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'you are to bring back this tree and place it as before in the garden of Nandana.'

notes: Blends the two cited variants as the pack's variant_notes describe: HV's conditional grant by Aditi (frame) with VP's planting in Satyabhama's garden (three-furlong scent, prior-existence memory). Nothing asserted contradicts either source. Source chronology note: HV places this homecoming after the reconciliation narrated in DKS_0233, so the corpus order 0232->0233 reads the resolution twice; each story individually matches its pack.

statements.claim: On the Parijatra mountain, in the first light, the battle over the tree began again, Krishna and Indra fighting from their cars while neither struck the other directly
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'there took place an encounter between those two celestials mounted on their cars on account of the Parijata... Indra did not strike Upendra in battle nor the latter the former.'

statements.claim: Krishna's arrows scattered Indra's soldiers, with ten sharpened shafts striking each of the horses of the king of gods
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'With straight-coursing arrows Vishnu... struck the soldiers of the king of gods... with ten sharpened arrows Janarddana struck each of the horses of the king of gods.'

statements.claim: Indra's arrows covered the horses of Krishna's car and buried Garuda's wings in shafts, while a thousand arrows cloaked the great elephant
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'Vasava... covered Shaiyya and other horses... With a thousand of arrows Krishna covered the elephant (of Indra) and the highly powerful slayer of Bali covered Garuda too.'

statements.claim: As the heroes fought, the earth shook like a boat adrift in water, the quarters blazed with lustre, mountains trembled, hundreds of trees were uprooted and pious mortals fell
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'the earth shook like a boat sunk in water and the quarters were fully enshrouded with lustre. Mountains shook, hundreds of trees were uprooted and pious mortals fell down on earth.'

statements.claim: Hurricanes blew, rivers ran backward, fire burned even in water, planets fought in the sky, hundreds of stars fell, and the elephants of the quarters quivered while cranes cried dreadfully overhead
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'hundreds of hurricane blew... the course of the rivers was changed in an opposite direction... fire was lighted even in the water and planets fought with planets in the sky. And hundreds of stars fell down on earth... Elephants of the quarters... began to quiver. The welkin was covered with cranes emitting loud cries.'

statements.claim: It seemed that earth, heaven, and sky had vanished from view
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'beholding those two heroic gods engaged in fighting with each other the earth, heaven and sky as if disappeared from view.'

statements.claim: The ascetics recited mantras and the brahmanas gave themselves to meditation, praying for the sake of all creatures
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'for the behoof of the world the ascetics began to recite Mantras and the Brahmanas speedily engaged in carrying on meditations.'

statements.claim: Brahma told Kashyapa: go with your wife Aditi and prevent your two sons
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'Brahma said to Kashyapa:—O you of firms vows, go with your wife Aditi and prevent your two sons.'

statements.claim: Seeing Kashyapa and Aditi in the battlefield, both heroes climbed down from their cars, laid down their arms, and saluted the feet of their parents
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'Beholding Kashyapa with Aditi in the battle-field those two heroic... got down from their cars, and leaving off their arms, saluted the feet of their parents.'

statements.claim: Aditi took both by the hands and said: born of the same parents you are trying to slay each other as if you were not brothers; let pass what has happened; if you obey your mother and father, lay down your arms and hear what I say
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'holding them both by the hands Aditi said:—Born of the same parents you are trying to slay each other as if you are not brothers. Let pass what has happened... lay down your arms and hear what I say.'

statements.claim: The two walked together to the bank of the Jahnvi river, where Indra said: O Krishna, you are the Lord and Creator of the universe and I have been placed by you in my kingdom; having accepted me as your elder brother, why do you wish to destroy me?
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'conversing with each other, went to the bank of the river Janhavi. Sakra said:—O Krishna, thou art the Lord Creator of the universe and I have been placed by thee in my kingdom... having accepted me as thy elder brother why dost thou wish to destroy me?'

statements.claim: The two bathed together in the Jahnvi, and the ascetics named the place the union ground of dear ones, where the brothers were united with their parents
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'having bathed in the water of the river Janhavi they both returned to... Kashyapa... and Aditi. The ascetics designate that place as the union ground of dear ones where those two lotus-eyed brothers were united with their parents.'

statements.claim: Krishna promised safety to Indra before the assembled celestials; the gods repaired to heaven, with Kashyapa, Aditi, Indra and Krishna riding together on one car, and Sachi adored the sage and his wife
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'after Krishna had promised safety unto Indra in the very presence of the pious celestials... seated on one car Kashyapa, Aditi, Indra and Upendra set out for the celestial region... Sachi... adored the high souled Kashyapa along with his wife.'

statements.claim: When the night had passed, Aditi gave the tree to Krishna to carry to Dwaraka for his wife's festival, on condition that it return to the garden of Nandana when the rite was done
statements.evidence: HV 1.222: 'after the night had elapsed Aditi... said to Hari... take this Parijata, go to Dwarka and perform the auspicious festival so longed for by your wife... you are to bring back this tree and place it as before in the garden of Nandana.'

statements.claim: The war ended not with a victor but with a mother's gift — the tree given, not taken — and the brothers went home at peace
statements.evidence: Interpretive close on the reconciliation and Aditi's gift.

notes: Fully grounded in HV 1.222, including the omens, both mothers' speeches, and the Jahnvi reconciliation. Note: in source order this episode precedes the homecoming narrated in DKS_0232, which the corpus runs immediately before it; each story matches its own pack.
